body:
I've been talking with some people, what I need to know to continue making this better is
* static storage for `const char*` unique strings that remain for the lifetime of the running program so that tracy can reference strings until application close. @Ivorforce and i were thinking StringName might hold some secrets I can use?
* more unique static storage for the gdscript SourceLocationData structs.

tracy just refers to elements stored elsewhere, it only creates the event tokens. when the profiler front end fetches the data from the application it first pulls all the event  tokens, and then pulls the storage items they refer to for names and such. At least that is my understanding.

By the way, something I forgot to note on the `profiling.h` header is that we should avoid including it in `.h` files. A really nice property of the current implementation is that adding / changing the profiler is a compile job of just ~30 seconds. If we start including `profiling.h` in headers, that might increase the compile cost a lot. 
So if at all possible, we should avoid including it in the gdscript headers.

> I've been talking with some people, what I need to know to continue making this better is
> 
> * static storage for `const char*` unique strings that remain for the lifetime of the running program so that tracy can reference strings until application close. @Ivorforce and i were thinking StringName might hold some secrets I can use?
> * more unique static storage for the gdscript SourceLocationData structs.

Thinking more about it, if tracy doesn't have support for `UTF32`, this won't work (since our strings are UTF32). We'd need to establish a new kind of interned string pool for UTF8. It might be worth it for profiling GDScript.
Alternatively, we could try to attach the UTF8 strings to GDScript instances somehow.

> tracy just refers to elements stored elsewhere, it only creates the event tokens. when the profiler front end fetches the data from the application it first pulls all the event tokens, and then pulls the storage items they refer to for names and such. At least that is my understanding.

I can't confirm or deny, but it would be interesting to know what tracy recommends doing. Allocating a new string for every call is certainly doomed to fail by bloat.

> I can't confirm or deny, but it would be interesting to know what tracy recommends doing. Allocating a new string for every call is certainly doomed to fail by bloat.

OK I went and looked at the manual to make sure. Turns out it is very explicit with how it handles strings. an abridged version is that if the macro expects const char * (no size), then it expects that storage to last for the lifetime of the program. and if it takes a const char* and size, then it will copy and not use it again thereafter.

But thats when using the macro's I dont like the idea of copying the same string from a gdscript function name billions of time if we can just store it once and refer to it. I'll look further into it.

OK so changes.
@Ivorforce I have managed to keep it out of headers, and removed all additions to the GDScriptFunction class.

I did end up creating that new class, but it has become so minimal that it might be worth just making it static functions in the profiling source files.

I'm not entirely done, I still have the sourcelocation data to fix. i'm just straight up new/delete and leaking it, took me ages to realise i had to save it, was tearing my hair out.
Also rad debugger is great.

OK, this is as good as I am probably going to be able to get. I tried really hard to avoid copying the strings, but I couldnt figure out a way to refer to a reference to tracy::SourceLocationData that doesnt crash, and I couldnt figure out why.

Tracy only provides either a constructor for a zone that copies the string data, or one that takes the address of SourceLocationData, so i had to stick with the one that copies since I couldnt figure out why it crashes.

Because tracy only takes char *, and godot strings are UTF32, I copied the StringName allocation and de-duplication code, and created the CharIntern class to compare and fetch any string that has been converted already. I wasnt sure if that would be any better than just performing the conversion each time since i have to copy the char* data anyway. But it turns out to be %30 faster in my tests. But there is(by design) no way to free the strings, so it should only be used in places that have predictable stable strings like the scripts. even so , it might not be worth it, since the time is only like ~5μs anyway.

Let me know if i should keep the CharString Interning, or anything else.
Cheers.

I was working on thread naming, and ran into the need to intern strings there too, which made me re-visit this after a day or so.
just fixing merge conflicts right now, but I removed the class object, and exercised some header sanitation. Just running the pre-commit hooks now.

You need to have some equivalent to `StringName::cleanup` for your interning, in order to empty out the `PagedAllocator` during shutdown, otherwise you'll end up running this `ERR_PRINT` during static destruction, which can crash the process due to [SIOF](https://en.cppreference.com/w/cpp/language/siof.html):

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/8deb2218292cc7b8de15616a13a0e76cf8edc04f/core/templates/paged_allocator.h#L167-L170

@mihe Thank you.

I'm just finishing up the pre-commit checks, that dotnet-format really takes its time, I cant tell if its just because I run it manually or what.

I YOLO'd the call for cleanup on all the platforms, because I dont really know where would be appropriate. I'm hoping that I can get some feedback here for where to place the call. I need a location as late as possible in in the lifecycle.

I also think that this should be gated behind an option, even if you're using gdscript, having _all_ of the calls profiled might not be desired. If anyone can provide some advice on the most appropriate way to make it optional, and some direction I can move this in that direction too.
Also thanks everyone for your patience.

Partially superseded by #113279.

The implementation of profiling the engine calls from GDScript added here was not included in https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/113279#issuecomment-3590622230 (to keep concerns separated and get the infrastructure merged early), so it would be good to have a follow-up PR redoing that missing part, for further review and hopefully merge for 4.6 to make the feature complete.
